Question: How many integers between \(1000\) and \(2000\) have all three of the numbers \(15,\) \(20,\) and \(25\) as factors?
Solution:
Having all three numbers as factors means being a multiple of all three. Their factorizations are
\[
15=3\cdot5,\qquad 20=2\cdot2\cdot5,\qquad 25=5\cdot5.
\]
A common multiple must contain two factors of \(2\), one factor of \(3\), and two factors of \(5\). Their product is
\[
2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot5=300.
\]
Conversely, \(300\) is divisible by \(15\), \(20\), and \(25\), so exactly the multiples of \(300\) qualify. In the requested interval these are \(1200\), \(1500\), and \(1800\). The adjacent multiples, \(900\) and \(2100\), are outside the interval, so the list is complete. There are \(\boxed{3}\) integers, choice \(\text{C}\).
